intro_script: Welcome to "Gear Up," your daily dose of robotics news. August 4th, 2026 - here's what's buzzing in the world of robotics today. From robot trade tensions between China and the US, to Unitree's promising first-half results and a breakthrough in autonomous ladder climbing, we've got you covered with our top stories.
outro_script: "Thanks for joining me in the workshop today! I hope you're not feeling too metal that we wrapped up already, but don't worry, the robot uprising will have to wait till tomorrow. Until then, stay charged and keep on robot-ing!"

items.title: China threatens retaliation after US restricts imports of new foreign-made humanoid robots
items.summary: China has threatened retaliation against US restrictions on foreign-produced humanoid robots, warning that the measures will damage economic and trade relations between the two countries. The US Federal Communications Commission added foreign-made advanced robotic devices to its Covered List, preventing new models from receiving necessary authorizations for import, marketing, and sale in the United States. China's Ministry of Commerce accused the FCC of ignoring Beijing's approach to product restrictions, warning that it would introduce countermeasures if the decision remained in place.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "China threatens retaliation after US restricts imports of new foreign-made humanoid robots." The US Federal Communications Commission has added foreign-made advanced robotic devices to its Covered List, effectively blocking the import and sale of new models in the United States. This decision was made by the FCC, which designated certain foreign-produced robotic devices as a security risk, thereby preventing them from receiving necessary authorizations for marketing, sale, and use within the US. As a result, Beijing has issued a statement accusing the FCC of ignoring China's approach to product restrictions, warning that it will introduce countermeasures if the decision remains in place.

items.title: Unitree expects first-half revenue growth as demand for humanoid robots accelerates
items.summary: Unitree Technology expects first-half revenue of about CNY1.1 billion ($156 million) for 2026, representing year-on-year growth of between 35.6 percent and 45.4 percent. The company plans to raise 4.2 billion yuan through its initial public offering (IPO), valued at more than 50 billion yuan, following regulatory challenges from the US Federal Communications Commission that may restrict future access to the US market.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Unitree expects first-half revenue growth as demand for humanoid robots accelerates". To support this ambitious target, the company plans to raise 4.2 billion yuan through an initial public offering (IPO), valued at more than 50 billion yuan, following regulatory challenges from the US Federal Communications Commission that may restrict future access to the US market. The IPO will allow Unitree to better navigate these challenges and expand its global presence.

items.title: Stepping Up: Figure 03 Achieves Autonomous Ladder Climbing, Reigniting the Bipedal Debate
items.summary: Figure 03's autonomous ladder climbing capability marks a significant milestone, utilizing advanced "loco-manipulation" and balance systems introduced in its Helix 02 software architecture. CEO Brett Adcock sharply criticizes wheeled robotics as an "utter dead end" due to environmental limitations like stairs and ladders. The robot's current pace is methodical but will eventually match human speed, addressing online critiques of the platform's agility.
items.audio_script:
From Humanoids Daily, "Stepping Up: Figure 03 Achieves Autonomous Ladder Climbing, Reigniting the Bipedal Debate". Figure 03 has successfully achieved autonomous ladder climbing capabilities, marking a significant milestone in its development. The robot's advanced locomotion and balance systems, introduced in its Helix 02 software architecture, enabled it to navigate complex staircases with ease.

The breakthrough was attributed to the integration of sophisticated "loco-manipulation" algorithms, which allowed Figure 03 to optimize its movement patterns and maintain stability on uneven surfaces. CEO Brett Adcock praised the achievement, stating that wheeled robotics had become an "utter dead end" due to environmental limitations like stairs and ladders. The robot's current pace is methodical but will eventually match human speed, addressing online critiques of the platform's agility.

Figure 03's autonomous ladder climbing capability reinvigorates the debate surrounding bipedal robots, with many experts now predicting a renewed focus on humanoid designs in robotics development.

items.title: Researchers unveil open-source robotic guide dog designed to assist blind and visually impaired people
items.summary: Researchers have unveiled Milo, the world's first fully autonomous robotic guide dog designed to assist blind and visually impaired people. The AI-powered robot can navigate both indoor and outdoor environments without requiring a prior 3D scan, using onboard artificial intelligence to identify paths and avoid obstacles. Milo can be manufactured for less than $2,000, making it a more accessible alternative to traditional guide dogs that cost tens of thousands of dollars.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Researchers unveil open-source robotic guide dog designed to assist blind and visually impaired people," a team of researchers has successfully created Milo, the world's first fully autonomous robotic guide dog capable of assisting blind and visually impaired individuals. Researchers have unveiled Milo, a low-cost alternative to traditional guide dogs that can navigate both indoor and outdoor environments without requiring a prior 3D scan. The AI-powered robot uses onboard artificial intelligence to identify paths and avoid obstacles, thanks to its advanced sensors and mapping capabilities. This breakthrough makes it possible for Milo to be manufactured for less than $2,000, offering improved accessibility to visually impaired individuals.

items.title: Former DeepMind team launches AI robotics startup with robots that learn from workers
items.summary: Reimagine Robotics, an AI robotics company founded by former Google DeepMind Applied Robotics team leaders, has emerged with technology that allows robots to learn from workers. The company's robots can be trained and used by anyone, without requiring specialist programmers. Workers can show the robot what to do, correct it on the spot, and move on to the next task, a process called 'monkey-see, monkey-do'.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Former DeepMind team launches AI robotics startup with robots that learn from workers". A new AI robotics company, Reimagine Robotics, founded by former Google DeepMind Applied Robotics team leaders, has emerged with technology that allows robots to learn from workers through a process called 'monkey-see, monkey-do'. The company's robots can be trained and used by anyone, without requiring specialist programmers. Workers simply show the robot what to do, correct it on the spot, and move on to the next task. This method enables efficient and effective collaboration between humans and robots, potentially transforming industries such as manufacturing and logistics.

items.title: How certified systems integrators reduce commissioning risk in robotic production cells
items.summary: Commissioning a robotic production cell requires testing across various systems, including robot controls, drives, safety functions, and plant networks. A qualified systems integrator reduces commissioning risk by treating these systems as one integrated system with documented acceptance criteria. This includes defining interfaces before the build, performing factory testing to expose logic and interface problems, and rechecking the cell in its final environment under site conditions.
items.audio_script:
From Robotics & Automation News, "How certified systems integrators reduce commissioning risk in robotic production cells." A certified systems integrator reduces commissioning risk by treating various systems as one integrated system with documented acceptance criteria, resulting in a lower likelihood of errors or issues during the testing phase.

A qualified systems integrator defines interfaces before the build, performs factory testing to expose logic and interface problems, and rechecks the cell in its final environment under site conditions. By following this process, these professionals can identify potential issues early on, allowing for efficient troubleshooting and resolution. This approach enables companies to establish a reliable robotic production cell that operates as intended. The outcome is a more streamlined commissioning process, reducing the risk of errors and ensuring a smoother start-up.

This methodology highlights the importance of partnering with experienced systems integrators who possess the necessary expertise to manage complex robotic production cells. By adopting this best practice, companies can minimize downtime and optimize overall production efficiency.

items.title: AI's next trade war: Robots
items.source: The Algorithm from MIT Technology Review
items.summary: The Federal Trade Commission has issued a sweeping ban on foreign imports of advanced robots, including humanoids, quadrupeds, and wheeled robots, citing national security concerns and the need to protect domestic robotics companies from Chinese competition. The decision aims to align political and industry interests and follows the Trump administration's aggressive approach to protecting the US AI industry.
items.audio_script: From The Algorithm from MIT Technology Review, "AI's next trade war: Robots," the Federal Trade Commission has issued a sweeping ban on foreign imports of advanced robots, including humanoids, quadrupeds, and wheeled robots. This decision stems from national security concerns and aims to protect domestic robotics companies from Chinese competition, aligning political and industry interests as part of the Trump administration's aggressive approach to safeguarding the US AI industry. The ban was achieved through a formal notice published in the Federal Register, outlining specific exemptions for existing imports and phasing out new shipments over time. This move is expected to significantly impact the global robotics market and have far-reaching implications for companies involved in robot manufacturing and development.

items.title: UK government launches £20 million funding competition for agricultural robots
items.summary: The UK government has launched a £20 million funding competition to support the development of agricultural robots and automation technologies, with the aim of improving productivity and reducing dependence on seasonal labor. The funding is available to agri-tech businesses working with researchers and farmers to develop robotic systems for planting, monitoring, and harvesting crops. The competition follows a recent £53 million funding package, bringing the total available this year to £123 million, and includes projects in livestock, forestry, and ornamental horticulture.
items.audio_script:
From Robotics & Automation News, "UK government launches £20 million funding competition for agricultural robots." The funding is available to support robotic systems for planting, monitoring, and harvesting crops, following a recent £53 million funding package bringing this year's total to £123 million. The competition includes projects in livestock, forestry, and ornamental horticulture, showcasing the government's commitment to supporting innovation in agricultural technologies. This initiative builds upon previous funding packages, further solidifying the UK's position as a hub for cutting-edge agri-tech development.

The launch of this funding competition marks an important milestone in the UK's efforts to harness AI and automation in agriculture, with potential benefits including increased efficiency, reduced labor costs, and improved crop yields.

items.title: Dubai and Oxa launch autonomous logistics venture to deploy self-driving vehicles at ports and airports
items.summary: Dubai Future Foundation and Oxa launch SHIFFT, a joint venture to deploy self-driving vehicles at ports and airports. The venture will utilize Oxa's autonomous technology to increase productivity, efficiency, and safety for customers, directly contributing to Dubai's goal of doubling foreign trade volume by 2033. SHIFFT aims to accelerate the commercialization of Oxa's Industrial Mobile Autonomy (IMA) technology, leveraging autonomy to unlock new levels of efficiency in major industrial environments.

items.title: The 1X Neo Robot Has Freaky Fast Fingers | WIRED
items.summary: 1X's Norwegian-American robotics company has unveiled its soft and helpful robot companion, Neo, with five-finger hands designed to replicate human hand movement. The hands have 25 degrees of freedom of movement, can grip odd shapes, detect slipping objects, and move extremely quickly. Neo's goal is full automation, but for now, it's partly teleoperated, allowing humans to remotely control the robot.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: Announcing protoros2: use protobuf in ros2 without compromise

items.summary: German robotics company Agile Robots expects to double its revenue this year, reaching approximately €600 million, after generating €300 million in 2025. items.title: Walden Robotics Partners With Toyota on Practical Humanoids
items.summary: Walden Robotics, a spinout from Toyota Research Institute (TRI), has emerged with $300 million in funding at a valuation of $1.1 billion, focusing on practical humanoid robots for manufacturing and logistics environments. The company's approach is centered around designing a robot that can safely and efficiently meet specific needs, skipping the legs to focus on higher payload requirements. Walden's partnership with Toyota provides a people-first culture that emphasizes improving quality of life, while also targeting high-utilization applications in manufacturing, making economics viable. The company aims to develop "multi-purpose" robots through leveraging previous learned skills, aiming for a general purpose robot platform.

items.title: NASA awards HEBI Robotics contract to develop compact robotic technology for small satellites
items.summary: HEBI Robotics has been awarded a Phase I contract from NASA's Small Business Innovation Research program to develop compact robotic actuators for use in small satellites and other space missions. The project aims to design miniature actuators that can generate high levels of force while remaining small enough for spacecraft with limited space and weight. The technology could be used in CubeSats and other compact spacecraft where existing robotic hardware is often too bulky or lacks flexibility.

This project aims to design miniature actuators that can generate high levels of force while remaining small enough for spacecraft with limited space and weight, addressing the issue of bulky or inflexible robotic hardware commonly found in CubeSats and other compact spacecraft. The technology development process involves a research and development phase focused on creating lightweight yet powerful actuators, utilizing innovative materials and designs to achieve these objectives.

items.summary: A Qualcomm-powered humanoid robot named 4NE-1 collapsed spectacularly on stage during a company's keynote at Computex 2026, triggered by a brief communication glitch. Stagehands quickly cloaked and carried off the stricken robot, which had been powered by Qualcomm's Dragonwing IQ10 robotics reference design.

items.title: Researchers develop control system that helps bird-inspired robots stay stable in windy conditions
items.summary: Researchers from Chiba University developed a control system that helps bird-inspired robots stay stable in windy conditions, overcoming unexpected movements and improving disturbance rejection by 53.1 percent. Flapping-wing robots are susceptible to wind gusts, but the new method accounts for their non-minimum-phase behavior, allowing them to maintain stable flight. The study could advance the development of small autonomous flying systems for inspection, monitoring, and search-and-rescue operations in confined spaces.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Researchers develop control system that helps bird-inspired robots stay stable in windy conditions." Researchers from Chiba University have developed a control system that enables bird-inspired robots to maintain stable flight in windy conditions. According to the study, this new method accounts for the non-minimum-phase behavior of flapping-wing robots, allowing them to better reject disturbances caused by wind gusts and improve stability by 53.1 percent. The development is an important step forward for small autonomous flying systems that could be used for inspection, monitoring, and search-and-rescue operations in confined spaces.

items.title: Track-Guided Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Vehicle Drifting with Minimum-Lap-Time Planning
items.summary: A planning-control framework is proposed for Minimum-Lap-Time (MLT) drifting in autonomous vehicles. The framework uses a Track-Guided Reinforcement Learning (TgRL) drift control method to learn a drift racing policy that optimizes both vehicle motion control and lap time reduction. The reward function incorporates an instant reward term and an end reward term derived from the MLT objective, allowing the agent to learn progressively from drift control policies to comprehensive drift race policies. Simulation results demonstrate effective learning of a drift racing policy that reduces lap times while maintaining vehicle motion control performance.

items.title: Motion Planning for Mobile Manipulators Navigating Doorways via Model Predictive Control
items.summary: A motion planning framework generates dynamically feasible and collision-free trajectories for autonomously opening and traversing both push and pull doors using a nonlinear Model Predictive Control (MPC) optimization framework. The robot and door are formulated as a coupled dynamical system, with manipulation feasibility enforced through a penalty-based constraint. Simulations and a hardware experiment demonstrate the approach's success in planning feasible trajectories for door traversal.

items.title: Developing Combined Manipulation and Locomotion Skills with Interaction Representation and Skill Composition
items.summary: Researchers Fanxing Meng and Jing Xiao developed a method to enable humanoid robots to learn combined manipulation and locomotion skills using interaction representation and skill composition. The approach learns a whole-body reaching and grasping policy via spatial convolution, followed by combining it with a separately learned getting-up policy to create a more complex policy. This results in a 93% zero-shot success rate for grasping unseen objects and a 96-100% success rate for standing up while holding the object.

items.title: Compliant Sphere Lattice Contact: Distributed Contact Modeling for Sphere-Based Robot Representations
items.summary: Researchers Nataliya Nechyporenko, Ava Abderezaei, and Alessandro Roncone introduced a distributed contact model called Compliant Sphere Lattice Contact (CSLC), which enables physically accurate contact modeling for sphere-based robot representations. CSLC models the robot interface as a compliant lattice of surface spheres connected through anchor and lateral springs, improving accuracy by producing a spatially distributed contact patch when pressed against an object.

items.title: Localization in Spatiotemporal Fields via Environmental PDEs
items.summary: A localization framework uses spatiotemporal fields governed by partial differential equations (PDEs) as signatures for vehicle localization. The PDE classes considered include the shallow water equations and the advection-diffusion equation, which model free-surface flows in coastal and riverine environments and transport and mixing of scalar quantities. A Rao-Blackwellized particle filter improves localization accuracy by fusing multiple field channels. Simulation studies demonstrate that this framework outperforms a standard particle filter in terms of final position error and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE).

items.title: Hybrid Attention Estimation Pipeline for Adaptive HRI Using an Expressive Robotic Head
items.summary: A hybrid attention estimation pipeline was developed for adaptive human-robot interaction (HRI) using an expressive robotic head based on the InMoov ecosystem. The pipeline combines a fast geometric perception layer with an independent semantic perception layer, providing high-frequency face and head-pose information and contextual attention labels. The system was evaluated in 40 trials across baseline and adaptive interaction conditions, showing reliable interaction start and non-redundant semantic information between outputs.

items.title: Action Chunk Scheduling for Batched Robot Policy Serving
items.summary: Researchers introduced the problem of serving robot policies to multiple robots from a remote GPU, formulating it as a scheduling problem. A proposed algorithm accounts for heterogeneity in action chunk consumption rates among robots and improves system throughput by up to 18%. The system, Armory, was validated on fleets of simulated and real robots, revealing that conventional batching methods are insufficient for closed-loop robot policy execution.

items.title: A Robotic System for Automated Manufacturing of Dielectric Elastomer Actuators
items.summary: A robotic system was developed to automate the manufacturing of dielectric elastomer actuators, specifically focusing on reducing process time and removing human operators. Twenty multilayer devices were fabricated with 12 dielectric layers and 11 alternating carbon nanotube electrodes, resulting in a 14.2% reduction in total process time and eliminating human involvement in 56.1% of the process.
